messages:
mara-support: Escalation from BrightDocs (acct bd-112). They expected ~12k objects to be purged by default 30d TTL but are still visible in search. Customer says they applied a custom retention tag 'litigation_preserve' on 2024-11-02 for a subset; they now want a preservation exemption until legal signs off. They've attached an API trace — delete calls returned 202 but objects remained. Asking for timeline and whether we can force-purge or pause deletes.

ben-infra: Can you paste the API trace + object metadata? Also need the region + KMS key id used for the objects.

mara-support: Pasting sanitized snippets below. Metadata shows "retention: litigation_preserve" for about 12k objects. KMS key: projects/redwood/locations/us/keyRings/prod/cryptoKeys/cust-bd-key. API trace: 
```
DELETE /v1/objects/bd-112/obj-000123 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Response: 202 Accepted
{ "id": "obj-000123", "status": "scheduled_for_deletion", "ttl": 0 }
```
But object still appears in search index and S3 storage after 48h.

devon-eng: 202 + scheduled_for_deletion is expected when we enqueue tombstone. Usually worker picks up and removes within minutes-hours. Two things to check: deletion-queue consumer logs and retention service decisioning (did it decide to skip due to active preserve?).

olga-security: Do we have a legal-hold flag or retention policy change audit for that customer? If they toggled a preserve tag, it should be recorded in audit logs and present in policy history. Also need to confirm KMS key rotation status (if HSM-backed and disabled, deletes might stall).

mara-support: Audit log snippet they attached: 
```
2024-11-02T16:02:18Z retention-service set_policy user=bob@brightdocs role=admin policy=litigation_preserve scope=bd-112
2024-11-02T16:02:20Z retention-service ack user=bob@brightdocs
```
No rotation events in provided logs.

retention-bot: EVENT: policy-applied bd-112 litigation_preserve by bob@brightdocs at 2024-11-02T16:02:18Z

devon-eng: OK can infra run a targeted repro: list one of the objects and run the deletion consumer in dry-run against it to see decision path. Example commands: 
```bash
# show metadata
redwoodctl objects get bd-112 obj-000123 --json
# simulate deletion consumer decision
bin/deletion-consumer --object-id obj-000123 --dry-run --log-level debug
```
We expect a log like: 
"decision=skip retention=litigation_preserve active=true reason=preserve_flag" or it will proceed to tombstone.

ben-infra: Running now against obj-000123. Output: 
```
2024-11-04T14:11:03Z INFO fetch-metadata id=obj-000123 retention=litigation_preserve expires=2025-12-01
2024-11-04T14:11:03Z DEBUG decision_table matched preserve_rule=litigation_preserve
2024-11-04T14:11:03Z WARN skip-delete id=obj-000123 reason=preserve_active
```
So the consumer is intentionally skipping deletion because the custom preserve policy is active. That explains why the object remains visible.

olga-security: Thanks — confirm whether the preserve policy was applied by customer or by our system. If customer requested it, legal needs to confirm deactivation before we purge. Also check if the policy was applied retroactively which could cause previously queued deletes to be aborted.

mara-support: Customer claims they toggled preserve consciously two weeks ago for "case-987". They now want a temporary exception for a subset of objects and for us to force-expire the preserve.

tess-legal: We need a formal preservation waiver request from BrightDocs signed by their counsel before we remove any preserve flags they set. If they provide explicit consent and the account owner confirms, we can schedule purge. Otherwise we must honor the preserve. Please ask BrightDocs legal to submit: 1) Signed waiver 2) list of object IDs 3) timeframe for deletion.

devon-eng: Technical note: if legal supplies waiver we can mark preserve=false and re-enqueue deletion; steps: 
1) run: redwoodctl retention update bd-112 --remove-policy litigation_preserve --requested-by legal-waiver-id
2) requeue objects: bin/requeue-deletes --batch-file ids.txt
3) monitor deletion-consumer logs and index re-sync.

ben-infra: If we need to force-purge without policy removal (legal approved but customer lacks UI access) we can run an override job that bypasses preserve rule, but that requires Security + Legal sign-off (audit trail will show override). Procedure: create an override ticket in the compliance audit system and include KMS key usage.

mara-support: I'll ask customer to provide signed waiver and list of IDs. Also asked them to confirm KMS key ownership. I've added the required checklist and CC'd legal.

olga-security: One more ops note: verify HSM key state. If the key is disabled/rotated and we cannot decrypt tombstones, deletes may be stalled at storage layer — check kms:cryptoKeys/cust-bd-key status.

ben-infra: I've checked KMS: key state=ENABLED, last_rotation=2024-06-01, no errors. So nothing blocking at KMS level.

tess-legal: Received a preliminary waiver PDF in thread. It names ids (sample) and authorizes removal. I'll validate and if OK will sign and upload to compliance portal.

mara-support: Great — next steps: waiting for signed waiver from Tess, then devon will run the retention update and requeue deletes. I'll keep customer updated.

devon-eng: Once waiver is in portal, ping me. I'll run a small pilot on 100 objects, watch index and storage. If pilot good, escalate to full batch.

tess-legal: Signed and uploaded. Waiver ID: WL-2024-289.

ben-infra: Requeue step executed for pilot (100 ids). consumer logs show deletions progressing, index refresh shows 100 objects removed after ~4 minutes.

mara-support: Customer confirmed pilot results match expectation and authorized full purge. Closing escalation after final run completes. :thumbsup:
